RTA_TARGET_BIN_HZ.doc: The RTA's target bin resolution — generated into `omx_contract_limits.h` as `OMX_RTA_TARGET_BIN_HZ`, which `mix_dsp.h` reads; the engine's conformance test reads it back from the header.

RTA_FFT_SIZE_MAX.doc: The largest RTA FFT the native ring holds — generated into `omx_contract_limits.h` as `OMX_RTA_FFT_SIZE_MAX`.

RTA_BAND_F_MIN.doc: The lowest frequency any spectrum band covers; below it is infrasonic and not drawn.

RTA_BAND_F_MAX_CAP.doc: The highest frequency any spectrum band covers, before the Nyquist clamp (omx_rta_band_f_max).

RTA_TIER_CROSSOVER_HZ.doc: A band centred below this samples the LOW (decimated) tier when the reading carries one; at or above it, the HIGH tier. Where the high tier's ~5.86 Hz bins still give ~51 bins per octave, above the finest panel's density.

RTA_BAND_GATE_DB.doc: Quiet gate of the band reduction: when no band rises above this, every band reads as silence, so a rig's idle floor never draws as a flat block. Keyed on the loudest band, not per band.

RTA_LEVEL_DB_MIN.doc: The floor of a spectrum display's level window: the bottom of the frame, every surface.

RTA_LEVEL_DB_MAX.doc: The ceiling of a spectrum display's level window: the top of the frame, where a band's peak reaching it draws a clip tick.

RTA_LEVEL_GRID_DB.doc: The spacing of a spectrum display's one dB graticule, from the ceiling down to the floor.

RTA_HZ.doc: How often a watched spectrum is read and published: an operator-cadence poll, never the audio thread.

RTA_LOW_ADVANCE.doc: How far the low zoom's window must have advanced, as a fraction of that window, before it is recomputed; between recomputes the last zoom rides the fresh main spectrum unchanged.

RTA_TAP_GATE_DB.doc: Quiet gate of a tap's raw spectrum, before any banding: when no bin rises above this the whole tap reads as the floor. The console's overlay frame applies it; a banded reading is gated by RTA_BAND_GATE_DB instead.

RTA_GRID_FREQS.doc: The frequencies of a spectrum display's labelled vertical graticule lines, Hz, on the log frequency axis: the decades and their 2 and 5 steps from 20 Hz to 20 kHz, every surface.

RTA_DELTA_DEADBAND_DB.doc: The smallest difference between two taps of a spectrum, POST - PRE in dB, that draws a wedge: a pair of neighbouring bands is a wedge when either band's difference reaches it. The console's overlay held it as 0.004 of its 100 dB span.
